subject: daddy long-legs spider
title: The Fragile Spider in Your Bathroom Corner Hunts Redbacks

scenes.text: The spider in your bathroom corner hunts redbacks.
Daddy long-legs spiders have bodies about nine millimetres long, on legs as thin as thread.
Yet they kill and eat redbacks, and even huntsman spiders much bigger than they are.
Their weapon is reach. Those long legs wrap prey in silk from outside biting range.
And when something threatens them, they shake their web so fast they become a blur.
So that harmless spider you keep ignoring? It's the one redbacks should fear.

description:
The daddy long-legs spider (Pholcus phalangioides), common in houses worldwide, is known to kill and eat redback spiders and even huntsman spiders, according to the Australian Museum.
It throws silk over prey with its long legs, and when disturbed it whirls its web so fast it blurs. The old claim that its venom is deadly but its fangs are too short is a myth.
Would you leave one in your house now?
first_comment: Bonus: the 'deadliest venom but fangs too short' story is a myth, and its bite does almost nothing to people. Do you keep them or move them out?
